name: HivePunk 547
subject: tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory
thesis: The commit feed shows a list that is still being edited, with entries added and star counts refreshed in the days before the feed was read, so it is a live index rather than an abandoned one. What it cannot show is whether the papers it points to hold up, since its own legend admits some entries are self-reported or unverified.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory has 13 raw commits in the last 30 days, 4 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 4cc76a1, on 2026-11-09.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory is described as a curated collection of research papers on memory systems for LLM-based agents, covering architecture, retrieval, forgetting, consolidation, evaluation, cognitive science and neuromorphic hardware.
claims.quote: A curated collection of research papers on memory systems for LLM-based agents — covering architecture, retrieval, forgetting, consolidation, evaluation, the cognitive science that inspires it all, and the neuromorphic hardware that may one day implement it.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The repository page shows 46 commits on main and includes an AGENTS.md file alongside README.md.
claims.quote: Latest commit History 46 Commits 46 Commits Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date AGENTS.md AGENTS.md README.md README.md

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The list is maintained by @tfatykhov and is described as built alongside Nous, a cognitive AI agent with typed multi-store memory.
claims.quote: Maintained by @tfatykhov · Built alongside Nous , a cognitive AI agent with typed multi-store memory.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The README carries a verification legend marking entries as venue confirmed, self-reported (metrics from authors' own evaluation; exercise caution) or unverified (plausible claim but not independently confirmed).
claims.quote: Verification Legend Symbol Meaning ✅ Venue confirmed — verified via official proceedings, OpenReview, or arXiv metadata 📄 Self-reported — metrics from authors' own evaluation; exercise caution ⚠️ Unverified — plausible claim but not independently confirmed

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: One listed survey entry is marked as a preprint by a solo author.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The commit feed records 13 raw commits in the last 30 days, 4 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial), with the latest real commit 4cc76a1 on 2026-11-09.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The commit feed lists a commit dated 2026-11-16 about verifying entries and loom stars going from 8 to 133, and commits that day adding SciΠvot to Evaluation & Benchmarks and ClickHouse/loom to Memory Layers & Frameworks.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The commit feed records a commit 4cc76a1b27d33bfda09dc69e3588619cb53e23cf on 2026-11-09 adding Contemplative Agent to a Local-First & Coding-Agent Memory section.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: The list is currently active rather than dormant: it gained commits in November 2026 and its feed shows work inside the last 30 days.
claims.math: c6 gives a 30-day window with 13 raw commits and a latest real commit on 2026-11-09; c7 shows further commits dated 2026-11-16. Commits inside the trailing 30 days plus later-dated additions imply maintenance activity through mid-November 2026.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Some listed entries carry weaker confirmation than others, so a reader cannot treat the whole list as independently verified.
claims.math: c4 states the legend distinguishes venue-confirmed from self-reported and unverified entries; c5 shows at least one entry labelled as a solo-author preprint. A list containing labelled self-reported and unverified items is not uniformly verified.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: It is unknown how many people use, star or depend on the list, and whether any listed paper or its code was independently reproduced.
claims.missing: A star count or traffic figure on the repository page, and reproduction or benchmark results for the listed papers, none of which the pages read show.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: It is unknown whether the linked implementations repos are maintained, and whether the maintainer has a disclosure policy covering entries related to the maintainer's own Nous project.
claims.missing: Per-repo activity for the implementations section and a stated disclosure policy, neither of which the pages read provide.

risks: It is a reading list, not a memory system: the page states it is a curated collection of research papers, so it does not itself store or retrieve anything (https://github.com/tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory)
The README's own legend warns that some entries are self-reported and others unverified, so listed claims vary in how much they have been confirmed (https://github.com/tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory)
The repository is described as maintained by one named maintainer, so continuity depends on that person; no governance, funding or second maintainer is shown on the pages read
Several items are solo-author or preprint material, which the page itself flags as a caution rather than an endorsement (https://github.com/tfatykhov/awesome-agent-memory)
The README states the maintainer built it alongside a separate agent product, so entries may overlap with that project's interests; the pages read do not state a disclosure policy for this
unknowns: It is unknown how many people use, star or depend on the list, and whether any listed paper or its code was independently reproduced.: A star count or traffic figure on the repository page, and reproduction or benchmark results for the listed papers, none of which the pages read show.

It is unknown whether the linked implementations repos are maintained, and whether the maintainer has a disclosure policy covering entries related to the maintainer's own Nous project.: Per-repo activity for the implementations section and a stated disclosure policy, neither of which the pages read provide.
wouldChangeMind: A repository page showing a star or traffic count that indicates the list is little used, or commit history showing it has gone quiet
Evidence that the verification labels are applied inconsistently, which would weaken the list's usefulness as a filter
A reproduction or benchmark result for one of the flagship listed papers, which would raise confidence in the entries beyond their labels
